name: Zhao Xiangti
current_role: Co-founder and former chairman, Yingde Gases Group (no confirmed current role found)
profile: Zhao Xiangti (赵项题) is a founding shareholder of Yingde Gases, once China's largest independent on-site industrial gas supplier (steel-mill oxygen/nitrogen plants), where he previously oversaw finances and later became chairman. He left the chair in 2017 after a shareholder vote; Yingde was then taken private by PAG. Current activities are not publicly documented.
interesting_fact: Yingde Gases, which he co-founded around 2001 with Sun Zhongguo and Trevor Strutt, grew into China's leading independent industrial-gas supplier to steelmakers and listed in Hong Kong.
notes: Low public profile; English coverage is mostly about the 2016-17 Yingde boardroom dispute (avoid in outreach). MarketScreener lists a Xiang Ti Zhao who led Torch's investment in Yingde, but it is unclear if that is the same person. Yingde is now private (PAG-owned), so no IR route to him.

name: Mustak Hossain
current_role: Chairman, Pataka Group (MD, Pataka Industries Pvt Ltd), Kolkata
profile: Mustak Hossain leads Kolkata-based Pataka Group, founded in 1952 by Giasuddin Biswas as a single biri factory in Murshidabad. Joining in 1980, he diversified it into tobacco, packaged tea and biscuits, textiles (East End Silks), healthcare and real estate (Pataka Infracorp).
interesting_fact: By 1998 Pataka had become India's largest biri maker and marketer, selling over 100 million sticks a day; it entered packaged tea with Pataka Tea in 2000.
deep_cut_fact: The group's philanthropic arm, GD Charitable Society (set up 1989), named after founder Giasuddin Biswas, went on to establish the GD Hospitals and Diabetes Institute in Kolkata in 2007.
notes: Country field blank in input; he is India-based (Kolkata). Low media profile; route via group head office (Pataka House, Mirza Ghalib St, Kolkata) or the contact page.

name: Sudhir Dhingra
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, Orient Craft Ltd (Gurugram)
profile: Sudhir Dhingra founded Orient Craft, one of India's largest garment exporters, supplying global fashion brands from factories around Gurugram. A law graduate from a Punjab cotton-farming family, he started exporting shirts in the 1970s and registered Orient Craft in 1978. The company has since rebuilt, declared itself debt-free and is expanding to Jharkhand.
interesting_fact: He told Outlook Business he wanted Orient Craft to be 'a 32-legged animal' that never depends on a single client; by 2014 it had revenue over Rs 1,151 crore and 30,000+ employees.
deep_cut_fact: Raised in Fazilka near the Pakistan border, he studied law like his father and grandfather; after a 1972 US trip a London trader friend asked him for 1,000 'cheese cloth' shirts, made in Delhi at Rs 15 each - the Rs 15,000 he calls his 'seed capital'.
notes: Company site orientcraft.com was unreachable when checked; recent press releases (Newsvoir, May 2024+) cover the debt-free turnaround and Jharkhand/Ranchi expansion - a positive hook. Avoid the NPA/debt history.

name: Rituraj Kishore Sinha
current_role: Group Managing Director, SIS Limited (Security and Intelligence Services India)
profile: Rituraj Kishore Sinha runs SIS, the security, facility-management and cash-logistics group founded by his father R.K. Sinha. After UK banking, he joined in 2002, led India's first private-equity deal in the security sector (2007), 12 acquisitions and the 2017 IPO, and became Group MD in 2017; revenue grew from Rs 25 crore to ~Rs 15,982 crore (FY2026).
interesting_fact: SIS was the first company in India's private-security sector to list on the stock exchanges (2017); under him it has expanded heavily abroad, notably in Australia.
deep_cut_fact: A Doon School alumnus with a Leeds BBA and LBS MBA, he chaired FICCI's Private Security Sector Committee (2014-22), sits on the board of the Swiss-based International Security Ligue and IIM Bodh Gaya, and lists a keen interest in wildlife.
notes: Also active in BJP politics (described as a BJP national secretary by Outlook India topic page) - same person. Data-center angle: SIS provides security/facility services to large campuses, a possible podcast hook.

name: Nicole Kidman
current_role: Actor and producer; founder of Blossom Films
profile: Australian-American actor (born Honolulu, 1967, raised in Sydney) and Academy Award winner for The Hours (2002). Her wealth comes from film and TV acting and producing; through Blossom Films (founded 2010) she has produced prestige TV such as Big Little Lies, and in 2024-26 she starred in Babygirl, Expats, The Perfect Couple, Special Ops: Lioness and Scarpetta.
interesting_fact: In 2024 she became the first Australian to receive the AFI Life Achievement Award, and won the Venice Volpi Cup for Best Actress for Babygirl the same year.
deep_cut_fact: She started ballet at age three and trained in drama and mime as a teen at Sydney's Phillip Street Theatre and the Australian Theatre for Young People; her first film role was the 1983 remake of Bush Christmas at 16. She has been a UNICEF goodwill ambassador since 1994.
notes: Entertainer, not an entrepreneur/energy figure; requests go through her talent agency/publicist (CAA / publicist) - not checked. Wikidata-sourced net worth only. Low fit for an energy/data-center podcast unless angle is Blossom Films as a business.

name: Paul J. Schneider
current_role: President, Schneider Resources (Green Bay family investment/operating company); director nominee/director, Schneider National (2026)
profile: Paul J. Schneider, 52, is a grandson of Schneider National founder Al Schneider and son of longtime CEO Don Schneider; he is one of five family members whose interests make up the voting trust controlling the trucking giant. He runs Schneider Resources, whose portfolio makes precision parts for aerospace and energy, and rejoined Schneider National's board in 2026 after serving 2020-22.
interesting_fact: He co-founded SLK Finance, a business-lending group, in 2011, and Schneider Resources' portfolio companies (e.g. JR Machine, Lindquist Machine) focus on precision parts for the aerospace and energy sectors - a direct energy-industry hook.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career as an M&A analyst at Morgan Stanley, held truckload, logistics and engineering roles at Schneider National, and holds a Northwestern economics BA, a Kellogg MBA and a master's in information systems from UW-Oshkosh; he sits on Northwestern University's board.

public_contacts.value: BoardofDirectors@schneider.com (Schneider National board; forwarded by Corporate Secretary)

notes: Private family figure; best routes are via Schneider Resources (Green Bay) or the Schneider National board mailbox. Energy/aerospace manufacturing portfolio is the natural podcast angle.

name: Jonathan M Jaffe
current_role: Retired Co-CEO & President of Lennar (retired 31 Dec 2025); board member, HomeAid America and other boards
profile: Jon Jaffe joined Lennar in 1983 and spent 42 years there, rising to COO (2004), President and Co-CEO; he led Lennar's 1995 expansion into California and the West and deals including CalAtlantic. He retired at the end of 2025 and left the board. An architect by training, he has served on boards incl. Five Point Holdings, Opendoor and True Anthem.
interesting_fact: He oversaw Lennar's acquisition and redevelopment of former military sites Mare Island, Hunters Point, El Toro and Treasure Island in California.
deep_cut_fact: Before homebuilding, he earned an undergraduate degree in architecture at the University of Florida and did graduate architecture studies at Georgia Tech.
notes: Retirement announced 14 Nov 2025 (https://investors.lennar.com/press-releases/2025/11-14-2025-222013161). Also listed on Millrose Properties insider filings. HomeAid (homeless-housing charity of the homebuilding industry) bio page is a warm, positive hook.

name: Zhao Jianhua
current_role: Co-founder and former CTO, China Sunergy (CEEG Nanjing PV-Tech); current role not confirmed
profile: Dr. Jianhua Zhao (赵建华), a UNSW-trained solar-cell scientist, worked with Martin Green's group in Sydney before returning to China in 2004 with fellow researcher Aihua Wang to co-found CEEG (Nanjing) PV-Tech, later Nasdaq-listed China Sunergy, where he served as CTO. Their equity in the company put them on the 2006 Hurun list.
interesting_fact: The world-record silicon solar cell that UNSW announced in 2008 as the first to reach 25% efficiency had been fabricated by Zhao and Aihua Wang before they left to build China Sunergy.
deep_cut_fact: As China Sunergy CTO he oversaw a monocrystalline production cell certified by Fraunhofer ISE at a then-record 20.26% efficiency; he and Wang won Australia's Advance Asia Impact Award in 2013 for their PV work.
notes: Strong energy/solar podcast fit (scientist-turned-founder). Identity inferred from Hurun shared listing with Wang Aihua and SEC F-1 exhibit naming Zhao Jianhua and Wang Aihua as shareholders (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1396247/000119312507090348/dex410.htm). China Sunergy is no longer listed; no current contact found. Advance award: https://advance.org/?p=1838

name: Anirudh Devgan
current_role: President and CEO, Cadence Design Systems; director, Lam Research
profile: Anirudh Devgan has been CEO of Cadence, the chip-design (EDA) software leader, since December 2021, succeeding Lip-Bu Tan. An IIT Delhi and Carnegie Mellon PhD, he spent ~12 years at IBM Research and seven at Magma Design Automation before joining Cadence in 2012. He is pushing Cadence into AI-driven design, system simulation and data-center digital twins.
interesting_fact: He received the 2021 Phil Kaufman Award, EDA's top honor, and was elected to the US National Academy of Engineering in 2023; he has said 'almost any chip designed in the world is done so with Cadence software.'
deep_cut_fact: Born in New Delhi in 1969 to an IIT Delhi professor, he holds 27 US patents, won best-paper awards at DAC and ICCAD, became an IEEE Fellow (2007) for electrical analysis and simulation of ICs, and chaired the American Heart Association's 2023 Heart of the Bay campaign.
notes: Excellent data-center fit: Cadence's Reality Digital Twin platform models data-center power/cooling, and it partners with NVIDIA. Frequent conference speaker.

name: Sachin Lawande
current_role: President and CEO, Visteon Corporation; independent director, Cognex
profile: Sachin Lawande has led Visteon, the Michigan-based automotive cockpit-electronics supplier, since June 2015, repositioning it around digital clusters, infotainment and in-vehicle compute (with NVIDIA and Qualcomm). Earlier he spent a decade at Harman International, rising to CTO and president of its infotainment division, after engineering roles at QNX, 3Com, U.S. Robotics and AT&T Bell Labs.
interesting_fact: In 2026 Visteon pushed beyond cars, launching D6Sigma, an edge-AI product line for industrial automation built with Qualcomm, and an edge-to-cloud AI platform for vehicles on NVIDIA technology.
deep_cut_fact: An engineer by training, he earned his bachelor's in electronics and telecommunications in India and a master's in electrical engineering at Southern Illinois University Edwardsville, and worked at AT&T Bell Labs and U.S. Robotics before moving into automotive software.
notes: Good AI-at-the-edge / compute angle. Undergrad institution given variously as Bombay University or Goa Engineering College - avoid naming it.

name: Richard A Hubbell
current_role: Executive Chairman, RPC, Inc. (oilfield services); formerly Executive Chairman, Marine Products Corp.
profile: Richard Hubbell is a longtime lieutenant of the Rollins family businesses in Atlanta. He was President of RPC, the oil-and-gas services company spun out of Rollins, from 1987 and CEO from 2003 until May 2022, when he became Executive Chairman; he also chaired boat maker Marine Products (Chaparral, Robalo).
interesting_fact: RPC (Cudd Pressure Control, Patterson Services and other units) provides pressure pumping, coiled tubing and other services to US oil and gas producers - a direct energy-industry link spanning nearly four decades of his leadership.
deep_cut_fact: He began with Rollins, Inc. in 1970 and was Executive Vice President of Rollins Communications, the family's media company, before moving to oilfield services; he holds an economics BA from Westminster College.
notes: Around 80 years old. RPC announced CEO Ben Palmer's retirement and a successor search in June 2026; Hubbell quoted as Executive Chairman. Input lists Marine Products Group as 'former' chairmanship (Marine Products appears to have changed ownership in 2026 - verify).

name: Thomas M Ryan
current_role: Operating Partner, Advent International; director, PJT Partners; URI Board of Trustees member (former Chairman/CEO, CVS)
profile: Tom Ryan started at CVS as a pharmacist after graduating from the University of Rhode Island College of Pharmacy in 1975 and rose to Chairman, President and CEO (1998-2011), leading the Caremark merger that created CVS Caremark. He is now an operating partner at private-equity firm Advent International and a board member at PJT Partners and (until 2026) Five Below.
interesting_fact: In 2019 he and his wife Cathy gave URI $35 million, the largest private gift in the university's history, including $24 million for the George & Anne Ryan Institute for Neuroscience they founded in 2013.
deep_cut_fact: He helped fund URI's Ryan Center arena (opened 2002), has sat on URI's Board of Trustees since its inception, chairs its Student Life and Athletics Committee, and chaired the search committees that picked URI's last two presidents.
notes: PJT Partners bio indicates his Five Below directorship ran 2011-2026, so he may have left that board. Avoid the Alzheimer's family backstory. Best warm route: URI or Advent International.

name: Marc S. Pritchard
profile: Marc Pritchard has spent 40+ years at P&G, joining in 1982 from Indiana University as a cost analyst and becoming global marketing officer in 2008 and Chief Brand Officer, overseeing the world's largest ad budget. He is known for pushing digital-media transparency, ad-industry reform and brand-purpose campaigns; he chaired the Association of National Advertisers for nearly a decade until 2025.
interesting_fact: He is an inductee of the Advertising Hall of Fame and stepped down as ANA chair in October 2025 after nearly ten years leading the US advertisers' trade body.
deep_cut_fact: Raised partly in Elkhart, Indiana ('mobile home capital of the world'), his first jobs were bussing tables, washing cars and working in mobile-home furniture and truck-cap factories; at P&G he started in cost analysis for Charmin, Bounty and Puffs, shelving plans for grad school.
notes: Corporate executive (wealth from P&G equity). Frequent keynote speaker (Cannes Lions, ANA). Route via P&G corporate communications.
